scope: Theorem 7.10 (Common conditional kernels on fixed charts) of the manuscript “Metric-measure limits of subcritical FK and spanning-tree planar maps” (preprints/Metric-measure-limits-of-subcritical-FK-and-spanning-tree-planar-maps-September-24-2026/main.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 211 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 1dd659698d3a3fde), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 55. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: Fix a finite collection of protected time charts, fixed instructions, and measurable E-valued observations of their raw words and exact parameters. Extract their independent reference experiments jointly as in Equation (7.5). Consider either the bilateral inventory word or a finite word conditioned to be empty. In the finite case keep every chart in a strict interior time interval. Use the same time and distance units in the reference and actual experiments. In every joint subsequential limit, conditional on the complete limiting contours, the retained cuts and marks locating the charts, and any independently adjoined surface-coordinate data, the observations have the reference kernels evaluated at their chart inputs. For charts in disjoint spatial buffers these kernels are conditionally independent. The assertion includes the universal endpoint observations, not only existential path certificates.
